Main.sentence: The contiguous United States , also known as the U.S. mainland , officially referred to as the conterminous United States , consists of the 48 adjoining ___E:U.S. states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state)___ and the ___E:District of Columbia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_of_Columbia)___ of the ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ in central ___E:North America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America)___ .

The term excludes the only two non- ___E:contiguous U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geographic_contiguity)___ states and the last two to be ___E:admitted to the Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admission_to_the_Union)___ , which are ___E:Alaska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska)___ and ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ , and all other offshore ___E:insular areas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insular_area)___ , such as the ___E:U.S. territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States)___ of ___E:American Samoa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Samoa)___ , ___E:Guam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam)___ , the ___E:Northern Mariana Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Mariana_Islands)___ , ___E:Puerto Rico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico)___ , and the ___E:U.S. Virgin Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Virgin_Islands)___ .
The colloquial term Lower 48 is also used, especially in relation to Alaska.
The term The Mainland is used in ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ .

The related but distinct term continental United States includes ___E:Alaska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska)___ , which is also in North America, but separated from the 48 states by ___E:British Columbia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia)___ in Canada, but excludes ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ and all the insular areas in the ___E:Caribbean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean)___ and the ___E:Pacific U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean)___ .

The greatest distance on a ___E:great-circle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great-circle_distance)___ route entirely within the contiguous U.S. is 2,802 miles (4,509 km), coast-to-coast between ___E:Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida)___ and ___E:Washington state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state))___ ;  the greatest north–south line is 1,650 miles (2,660 km).
The contiguous United States occupies an area of 3,119,884.69 square miles (8,080,464.3 km 2 ).
Of this area, 2,959,064.44 square miles (7,663,941.7 km 2 ) is actual land, composing 83.65 percent of the country's total land area, and is comparable in size to the area of Australia.
Officially, 160,820.25 square miles (416,522.5 km 2 ) of the contiguous United States is water area, composing 62.66 percent of the nation's total water area.

The contiguous United States, if it were a country, would be fifth on the ___E:list of countries and dependencies by area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area)___ , behind ___E:Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia)___ , ___E:Canada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada)___ , ___E:China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China)___ , and ___E:Brazil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil)___ .
However, the total area of the United States, including Alaska and Hawaii, ranks third or fourth.
Brazil is 166,000 square miles (431,000 km 2 ) larger than the contiguous United States, but smaller than the entire United States including Alaska, Hawaii and overseas territories.

The ___E:2020 U.S. census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census)___ population of the area was 328,571,074, comprising 99.13 percent of the nation's total population, and a density of 111.04 inhabitants/sq mi (42.872/km 2 ), compared to 93.844/sq mi (36.233/km 2 ) for the nation as a whole.

While conterminous U.S. has the precise meaning of contiguous U.S. (both adjectives meaning "sharing a common boundary"), other terms commonly used to describe the 48 contiguous states have a greater degree of ambiguity.

Because ___E:Alaska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska)___ is also a part of ___E:North America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America)___ , the term continental United States also includes that state, so the term is qualified with the explicit inclusion of Alaska to resolve any ambiguity.

On May 14, 1959, the ___E:United States Board on Geographic Names U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Board_on_Geographic_Names)___ issued the following definitions based partially on the reference in the Alaska Omnibus Bill, which defined the continental United States as "the 49 States on the North American Continent and the District of Columbia..." The Board reaffirmed these definitions on May 13, 1999.  However, even before Alaska became a state, it was properly included within the continental U.S. due to being an ___E:incorporated territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States#Incorporated_vs._unincorporated_territories)___ .

The term mainland United States is sometimes used synonymously with continental United States , but technically refers only to those parts of states connected to the landmass of North America, thereby excluding not only ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ and overseas ___E:insular areas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insular_area)___ , but also islands which are part of continental states but separated from the mainland, such as the ___E:Aleutian Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleutian_Islands)___ ( ___E:Alaska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska)___ ), ___E:San Juan Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Juan_Islands)___ ( ___E:Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state))___ ), the ___E:Channel Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_Islands_(California))___ ( ___E:California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California)___ ), ___E:the Keys U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Keys)___ ( ___E:Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida)___ ), the ___E:barrier islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrier_island)___ ( ___E:Gulf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Coast_of_the_United_States)___ and ___E:East Coast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Coast_of_the_United_States)___ states), and ___E:Long Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island)___ (New York).

CONUS , a technical term used by the ___E:U.S. Department of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense)___ , ___E:General Services Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Services_Administration)___ , ___E:NOAA/National Weather Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Oceanic_and_Atmospheric_Administration)___ , and others, has been defined both as the continental United States, and as the 48 contiguous states.
The District of Columbia is not always specifically mentioned as being part of CONUS .
OCONUS is derived from CONUS with O for outside added, thus referring to Outside of Continental United States.
The term lower 48 is also used to refer to the conterminous United States.
The National Geographic style guide recommends the use of contiguous or conterminous United States instead of lower 48 when the 48 states are meant, unless used in the context of Alaska.
Almost all of Hawaii is south of the southernmost point of the conterminous United States in Florida.

During ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ , the first four ___E:numbered Air Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Numbered_Air_Force)___ of the ___E:United States Army Air Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Air_Forces)___ (USAAF) were said to be assigned to the Zone of the Interior by the American military organizations of the time—the future states of ___E:Alaska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska)___ and ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ , then each only ___E:organized incorporated territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organized_incorporated_territories_of_the_United_States)___ of the Union, were respectively covered by the ___E:Eleventh Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleventh_Air_Force#Origins)___ and ___E:Seventh Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh_Air_Force#Origins)___ during the war. [citation needed]

Residents of Alaska, Hawaii and off-shore ___E:U.S. territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States)___ have unique labels for the contiguous United States because of their own locations relative to them.

The vast territory of ___E:Alaska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska)___ became the 49th state of the United States on January 3, 1959. Alaska is the northwest extremity of the North American continent, separated from the ___E:U.S. West Coast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Coast_of_the_United_States)___ by the ___E:Canadian province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_and_territories_of_Canada)___ of ___E:British Columbia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia)___ .

The term Lower 48 has, for many years, been a common Alaskan equivalent for "contiguous United States";   some Alaskans may use the term Outside for those states, though some may use Outside to refer to any location not within Alaska.

The territory of ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ , consisting of the entire ___E:Hawaiian Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiian_Islands)___ archipelago except for ___E:Midway Atoll U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midway_Atoll)___ , [a] became the 50th state of the United States on August 21, 1959. It is the southernmost U.S. state, and the latest one to join the Union.

Not part of any continent, Hawaii is located in the ___E:Pacific Ocean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean)___ , about 2,200 miles (3,541 km) from North America and almost halfway between North America and ___E:Asia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia)___ .
In Hawaii and ___E:overseas American territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insular_area)___ , for instance, the terms the Mainland or U.S.
Mainland are often used to refer to the 49 states in North America.

Puerto Rico is an ___E:unincorporated territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unincorporated_territories_of_the_United_States)___ of the United States located in the northeast ___E:Caribbean Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea)___ , approximately 1,000 miles (1,609 km) southeast of ___E:Miami U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami)___ , ___E:Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida)___ .
Puerto Ricans born in Puerto Rico are U.S. citizens and are free to move to the mainland United States.
The term Stateside Puerto Rican refers to residents of any U.S. state or the District of Columbia who were born in, or can trace their family ancestry to, Puerto Rico.

The ___E:U.S. Virgin Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Virgin_Islands)___ is a ___E:U.S. territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States)___ located directly to the east of Puerto Rico in the Caribbean Sea.  The term stateside is used to refer to the mainland, in relation to the U.S.
Virgin Islands  (see ___E:Stateside Virgin Islands Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stateside_Virgin_Islands_Americans)___ ).

___E:American Samoa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Samoa)___ is a ___E:U.S. territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States)___ located in the ___E:South Pacific Ocean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Pacific_Ocean)___ in ___E:Polynesia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynesia)___ , south of the equator — it is 2,200 miles (3,500 km) southwest of ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ .
In American Samoa, the contiguous United States is called the "mainland United States" or "the states"; those not from American Samoa are called palagi (outsiders).

Apart from off-shore ___E:U.S. islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_of_the_United_States_by_area)___ , a few continental portions of the contiguous United States are accessible by road only by traveling through Canada. ___E:Point Roberts, Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_Roberts,_Washington)___ ; ___E:Elm Point, Minnesota U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elm_Point,_Minnesota)___ , and two nearby points; the ___E:Northwest Angle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Angle)___ in ___E:Minnesota U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota)___ ; a peninsula in ___E:Osthus Lake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Osthus_Lake&action=edit&redlink=1)___ in ___E:North Dakota U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Dakota)___ 's ___E:Rolette County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolette_County,_North_Dakota)___ and a slice of land on the edge of ___E:Lake Metigoshe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Metigoshe)___ in ___E:Bottineau County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bottineau_County,_North_Dakota)___ bordering ___E:Winchester, Canada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipality_of_Deloraine_%E2%80%93_Winchester)___ , are seven such places. ___E:Alburgh, Vermont U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alburgh_(town),_Vermont)___ , is not directly connected by land to the rest of the contiguous US, but is accessible by road via bridges from within Vermont and from New York, and nearby ___E:Province Point U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_Point)___ is accessible over land only from Canada, though no roads go there.

In contrast, ___E:Hyder, Alaska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyder,_Alaska)___ , is physically part of contiguous Alaska and is its easternmost town, but the only practical overland access is by road through Canada.
